# ceryx_route (Resource)

A Ceryx route: requests whose `Host` header (or TLS SNI) is `source` are proxied or redirected to `target`. Creating a route that already exists in Ceryx fails, so an existing route is never overwritten; import it instead.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ceryx_route" "app" {
  source        = "app.example.com"
  target        = "http://app:8000"
  enforce_https = true
}

resource "ceryx_route" "www" {
  source = "www.example.com"
  target = "https://app.example.com"
  mode   = "redirect"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `source` (String) Host name the route matches, for example `app.example.com`. `$wildcard` is the fallback route for hosts with no route of their own. Changing it replaces the route.
- `target` (String) Where requests go, for example `http://app:8000`. Ceryx resolves host names with its own DNS resolver, usually Docker's.

### Optional

- `certificate_path` (String) Path, inside the Ceryx container, to a TLS certificate for `source`. Unset, Ceryx uses Let's Encrypt or its default certificate.
- `enforce_https` (Boolean) Redirect plain HTTP requests to HTTPS. Defaults to `false`.
- `key_path` (String) Path, inside the Ceryx container, to the private key for `certificate_path`.
- `mode` (String) `proxy` forwards requests to `target`; `redirect` answers with a redirect to it. Defaults to `proxy`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import ceryx_route.app app.example.com
```
